35. Regarding liability:
As stated above the respondent No.1 have proved that they have not issued the policy for the offending vehicle/Auto as on the date of accident.

As per settled principle of law if the offending driver had no valid driving licence and even  (SCCH3) 24 MVC.No.6767/19  c/w MVC.No.6768/19 violated any of the policy conditions, then the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the victims/third party and then to recover from the R.C owner.
But in the instant case as the respondent No.1 have not issued policy to the respondent No.2

,
then they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

It is true that the petitioners have proved that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Auto bearing No.
KA03B5300.
It is also true that as on the date of accident there was no valid driving licence for the offending auto driver which had caused accident.

Hence in the instant case looking into the facts and circumstances of case the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation as he had no valid policy and driving licence on the date of accident.

So on perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation has filed chargesheet against the Auto driver and owner of auto as accused No.1 and 2 for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 337, 338 of IPC and Sec.187 and Sec.181(3) of  (SCCH3) 15 MVC.No.6767/19  c/w MVC.No.6768/19 IMV Act for the reason that the driver of auto after causing the accident left the auto and fled away from the accident spot.
Even the chargesheet is filed against the owner of auto who had entrusted the vehicle to the driver who was not having valid driving licence to drive such type of vehicle.
22 . Hence from the police records it is true that the offending auto had no valid driving licence and also policy as on the date of accident.
It is not for the insurance  (SCCH3) 16 MVC.No.6767/19  c/w MVC.No.6768/19 company to prove that the vehicle is not insured with them.
N V/s Iffco Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.,
and another - It is observed that when the claimant has not made any effort to place record to demonstrate that the policy was issued by the insurance company then in absence of acceptable evidence in respect of issuance of policy then there is no liability on part of insurance company.
 c. MFA No.675/2020 (WC) - The Branch Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Smt.Rathnamma and another - It is observed that when there is no policy then no liability on part of insurance company.
d. MFA No.5044/2009 (MV) - Branch Manager,
National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Shivalingegowda @
Shivalinga and another - It is observed that when there is no policy then no liability on part of insurance company.
27. Even the petitioner has stated that due to the accident he had sustained disability.
In this regard the petitioner has not adduced any evidence of the doctor to show his disability.
It is pertinent to note that the petitioner has not produced any document to show his avocation, income and loss of income.
Even there are no documents to show that due to the accident the petitioner is not able to do any work and to earn income in future.
Hence the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income.
Even there are no documents on record to show that the petitioner required future treatment and expenses.
Hence under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of future medical expenses.

As per settled principle of law if the offending driver had no valid driving licence and even  (SCCH3) 24 MVC.No.6767/19  c/w MVC.No.6768/19 violated any of the policy conditions, then the Insurance Company is liable to pay the compensation to the victims/third party and then to recover from the R.C owner.
But in the instant case as the respondent No.1 have not issued policy to the respondent No.2
It is true that the petitioners have proved that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of Auto bearing No.
KA03B5300.
It is also true that as on the date of accident there was no valid driving licence for the offending auto driver which had caused accident.
Hence in the instant case looking into the facts and circumstances of case the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation as he had no valid policy and driving licence on the date of accident.
